AI strategy, generative AI, enterprise and digital transformation

jobs.title: Vice President, AI Strategy & Product Management
jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service North American-based financial services provider, with over 2,700 professionals in 30 locations around the world, including 20 offices in North America, offering corporate, institutional and government clients access to a complete range of investment and corporate banking products and services. BMO Capital Markets is a member of BMO Financial Group (NYSE, TSX: BMO), one of the largest diversified financial services providers in North America with US$1.0 trillion total assets and approximately 54,000 employees as of January 31, 2025.

What is the opportunity?

The Data Cognition Team (DCT) is BMO Capital Markets’ AI engineering and enablement team, with nearly a decade of experience building and deploying AI solutions in complex, regulated financial services environments.

As Vice President, AI Strategy & Product Management, you will operate at the intersection of business strategy, product management, and AI. You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap, delivery, and adoption of high-value AI and data products, working closely with front-office users, senior leaders, engineers, data scientists, UX, risk, and compliance partners.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, influence, and hands-on product leadership required to scale trusted AI and data products and capabilities in a highly regulated Capital Markets environment.

What will you do?

Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, investment priorities, and business outcomes for one or more AI-enabled products or capabilities supporting Capital Markets users and workflows.
Develop a deep understanding of front-office and business needs; translate strategic pain points into clear product opportunities.
Lead product discovery, experimentation, and investment decisions, including prototypes, proofs of concept, and minimum viable products, to validate assumptions before scaling.
Align senior business, technology, data, and control-function stakeholders around product priorities, trade-offs, risks, and expected outcomes.
Establish product goals and success measures, monitor adoption and performance, and use quantitative and qualitative insights to improve products and demonstrate business impact.
Present product recommendations, performance, risks, and strategic choices to senior leadership and governance forums.
Apply Responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, model risk, and regulatory considerations throughout the product lifecycle in partnership with control functions.

What do you need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in a related field; an advanced degree or relevant professional designation is an asset.
6+ years of relevant experience in product management, strategy, digital transformation, or technology delivery, ideally within Capital Markets or financial services; familiarity with AI and data product management is an asset.
Ability to understand complex Capital Markets workflows and translate between business users and technical teams; direct experience with sales, trading, research, banking, or client-coverage workflows is an asset.
Hands-on familiarity with AI and LLM-enabled products, including retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation, and production deployment considerations.
Strong written and verbal communication, analytical judgment, structured problem-solving, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to develop informed perspectives on the evolving AI landscape, including emerging technologies, industry trends, and market practices, and translate relevant developments into strategic implications and opportunities for BMO Capital Markets.

$120,000-$150,000 CAD

(subject to negotiation and subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements)

jobs.title: Director, Delivery CX AI
jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Compensation Range: CA$150K - CA$190K

jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering - CoCounsel Legal
jobs.description:
Job Description

CoCounsel Legal is Thomson Reuters' AI assistant for legal professionals. This role leads the part of it that makes it adaptable: the agent's ability to take on a customer's skills, connect to third-party systems, and remember what matters to each legal team.

As Director, you will lead multiple engineering teams building the core of the CoCounsel Legal product. Your teams will let law firms and corporate legal departments add their own skills, connect their own tools through MCP integrations, and make CoCounsel work the way they do.

You will also contribute directly to the agent itself. This work carries high stakes for confidentiality, permissions, and customer control, and you will make the security and architecture decisions that earn customer trust.

We want an AI-native engineering leader who works at the forefront of AI-assisted development. You already build with coding agents and agent workflows, and you set the standard for how your teams do the same. You stay hands-on, make sound technical trade-offs, and plan strategically while the product and customer needs are still taking shape.

This is a hybrid role based in one of our hub locations: Minneapolis/Eagan, Dallas, Toronto, or New York City. Hybrid means two to three days a week in the office, depending on the role.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop multiple engineering teams, and build the leadership layer (managers and technical leads) as the scope grows. Own workforce planning, hiring, performance, calibration, and succession.
Own the engineering vision and delivery for how customers extend CoCounsel Legal. This includes custom skills and the tools to create, test, version, share, and retire them.
Lead the design and delivery of MCP and third-party integrations, so customers can connect their own systems and tools to the CoCounsel agent safely and at scale.
Contribute directly to the CoCounsel agent, working with Agent Core and Science on how it uses skills, tools, memory, and context.
Own agent memory at the user and organization levels. Start narrow, prove each step with evidence, and expand.
Make customization safe for the enterprise. Own the security model for sharing and integrations, including least-privilege permissions, audit logging, and administrator controls. Lead the response to complex security and privacy issues, working with Security and Privacy.
Make evaluation a release gate. Work with Science and subject-matter experts so that skills and agent behavior are tested for quality, accuracy, and fidelity to customer instructions before they ship.
Set the technical direction. Decide what to build, buy, or partner on, favor reusable primitives over one-off features, and make clear trade-offs among speed, quality, security, and cost.
Set the standard for AI-native engineering. Define how your teams use coding agents and AI tools to build, review, and verify work, and model that practice yourself.
Stay hands-on. Spend at least 30% of your time on technical work such as design and code review, prototyping, and building with AI coding agents.
Build a culture of end-to-end ownership. Your teams design, build, deploy, and operate their services, including on-call, SLOs, and incident response. You take part in the escalation path for major incidents.
Measure outcomes, not activity. Use DORA metrics alongside quality and developer-experience measures, and fund the next stage of work through short, evidence-based checkpoints.
Own the investment envelope across people, cloud, AI inference, and vendor services.
Work directly with customers and Product, including beta customers. Explain engineering trade-offs clearly to business and executive stakeholders.
Partner with peers in Agent Core, Application Experience, Platform, and Corporate Integrations to keep CoCounsel coherent as a product.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of software engineering experience, including proven success leading multiple teams and leading through other managers or technical leads
Hands-on engineering work within the last two to three years, and the ability to contribute to design, code, and architecture
Hands-on experience building agentic systems or LLM-based agent features, such as tool use, prompt and instruction management, memory, retrieval, or context management, and a practical sense of where they fail
AI-native ways of working: daily, proficient use of AI coding tools and agent setups to do engineering work, and experience setting team norms for verifying agent-generated work
Experience building integrations with third-party systems, and experience with MCP or comparable tool and plugin protocols
Experience building platforms that customers configure and extend, such as skills, plugins, extension frameworks, or workflow and automation features
Strong backend foundation, including API design, authentication and authorization, multi-tenancy, versioning, data lifecycle, event-driven processing, and observability
Experience making sound technical trade-offs and resolving complex security issues, particularly where third-party access and customer data are involved
Experience evaluating agentic systems and building evaluation into the release process, working with science and subject-matter experts
Experience leading teams that operate what they build, with production on-call, SLOs, and incident response
Proven strategic planning: setting direction under ambiguity and re-planning based on evidence from working software and customers
Accountability for workforce planning, budget, and build-versus-buy decisions
Proficiency in Python and strong engineering fundamentals, including cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), CI/CD, and testing strategy
Understanding of the privacy, security, and compliance obligations of handling confidential and privileged customer data
Clear, persuasive communication with engineers, product partners, and senior business stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building agent memory, such as user and organization memory, memory search and inspection, and giving users and administrators control over what is kept
Experience building tools that let non-engineers create and improve agent behavior, such as skill or prompt authoring, test chats, and review workflows with versioning and rollback
Background in legal technology, or in enterprise software for legal, compliance, or risk functions, including customers who need confidentiality, ethical walls, and audit trails
Experience with enterprise administration and sharing models, such as groups, roles, org-level publishing, and usage reporting
Experience running customer beta programs and turning feedback into a path to general availability
Experience building a new product line alongside an established one, and organizing teams around shared platforms
Contributions to open-source agent, MCP, or developer-tooling projects

New Position: This position is open due to an existing vacancy to support our evolving business needs.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

Our use of AI within the recruitment process Thomson Reuters utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support parts of our global recruitment process. Unless you opt-out, our AI system will assess the information provided by you and compare it to the requirements listed for the role, and present the result to our recruitment personnel for further review. The AI system acts as a supporting tool, but there is always a human making the decision if you will be considered for the role.

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. Vice President, Treasury

Toronto, ON (On-Site)

This position is for an existing vacancy in a newly created role, as disclosed in accordance with the Ontario Employment Standards Act (ESA).

Company Overview:

Nexus Energy Inc. is a privately held energy company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, active in trading electricity across Eastern Canada, the Northeastern U.S., and Western markets, as well as providing power price risk management solutions to large commercial and industrial loads in Ontario. In addition, Nexus is actively working to develop a pipeline of renewable energy projects.

At Nexus, we foster a culture that values high performance, collaboration, and continuous development. You will join a passionate team that drives the business forward through innovation, accountability, and open communication.

Position Overview

Nexus Energy is seeking a Vice President, Treasury to build and lead its Treasury function. Reporting directly to the CEO, the VP will manage foreign exchange and interest rate exposures, execute hedging strategies, and oversee liquidity, banking relationships, and treasury operations.
The VP will partner with Trading, Finance, Settlements, and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to manage financial exposures and develop treasury processes and controls that support growth. Treasury will operate within the company’s Risk Policy and risk appetite, which are governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

We welcome senior corporate treasury professionals and senior banking or capital markets professionals with corporate advisory experience in hedging, funding, or liquidity. The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

What You Will Do

Foreign Exchange(FX) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring, and management of the company's foreign exchange exposures. Ensure FX exposures are managed appropriately in line with the company's Risk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate and execute appropriate FX hedging instruments and strategies, including forwards, swaps, options and structured hedging solutions, where appropriate to mitigate exposures arising from trading activities, operational cash flows, cross-border transactions and foreign currency-denominated assets and liabilities.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific FX risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor currency market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material FX risks, market conditions and potential hedging opportunities.

Interest Rate (IR) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring and management of the company's interest rate exposures across its balance sheet and financing activities, in accordance with the company'sRisk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate the impact of changing interest rate environments on the company's financing costs, cash flows, liquidity and overall financial position.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific interest rate risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor interest rate market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material IR risks and provide strategic advice on interest rate positioning, hedging alternatives and financing considerations.

Balance Sheet Liquidity & Cash Management
Collaborate with Finance, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to monitor cash positions, funding requirements and liquidity buffers across the company's banking relationships and legal entities, ensuring sufficient liquidity to support ongoing trading activities, operational requirements and strategic initiatives.
Work closely with Finance, Trading, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to anticipate material cash flow requirements, settlement obligations and potential liquidity pressures, developing and maintaining short-, medium- and long-term cash flow and liquidity forecasting frameworks.
Oversee liquidity requirements associated with trading activities, including collateral, margining, credit support arrangements and other working capital considerations.
Proactively identify opportunities to optimize cash utilization, funding efficiency, and returns on excess liquidity, as well as potential liquidity risks, and develop appropriate contingency funding and liquidity management plans.

Banking & Financial Institution Relationships
Own and manage the company's banking and financial institution relationships, acting as a primary point of contact for treasury-related matters. Develop strategic relationships with existing and potential banking partners, ensuring the company has access to appropriate banking products, credit facilities, and financial services.
Lead discussions and negotiations relating to banking arrangements, credit facilities, cash management solutions, trade finance, and other treasury-related services. Coordinate with senior leadership and the Finance team on financing requirements, facility renewals, credit negotiations, and broader funding initiatives.
Identify opportunities to diversify banking relationships, optimize banking costs, and improve access to financial products and services.
Advise the CEO and senior leadership on funding strategy and capital structure. Evaluate financing alternatives, including new or expanded credit facilities, to support trading activity, working capital, and business growth.
Partner with Finance and Legal to assess financing terms, collateral requirements, and covenant implications, and support the execution of approved financing initiatives.

Strategic Advisory & Risk Management Governance
Act as the company's senior treasury subject matter expert and provide strategic advice to the CEO and senior leadership on FX, interest rate, liquidity, and broader financial risk management matters, and recommend appropriate financial risk mitigation solutions that balance commercial objectives, risk tolerance, and market conditions within the company'sRisk Policy framework as defined and governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Work collaboratively with Risk &Regulatory Affairs, providing treasury and financial markets expertise to support the development, implementation, and ongoing maintenance of the company's Risk Policy, including financial risk exposures, hedging strategies, risk metrics, and practical risk management considerations. Overall Risk Policy ownership and governance will remain with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

Cross-Functional Risk Identification & Management

Collaborate with Trading and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to understand current and anticipated trading positions, transaction structures, forecast cash flows, and associated FX and interest rate exposures, including financial risk and hedging considerations relating to customer transactions.
Work with Finance and Settlements to identify balance sheet exposures, financing requirements, foreign currency liabilities and other financial risks, ensuring timely identification of settlement-related exposures, currency requirements, cash movements and potential liquidity mismatches.
Partner with Risk &Regulatory Affairs to support the monitoring and management of financial risk exposures and associated hedging activities, providing treasury expertise and execution support as required.

Establish and develop the company's treasury function, including the implementation of appropriate processes, systems, controls and reporting infrastructure. Assess existing treasury-related workflows and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, transparency, consistency and risk oversight.
Develop standardized processes for exposure identification, hedge execution, trade capture, confirmation, settlement, reconciliation and ongoing monitoring.
Work collaboratively with Finance and Settlements to strengthen internal treasury knowledge and capabilities. Cross-train and upskill existing Finance team members in treasury operations, FX and interest rate risk management, financial instruments and hedging methodologies.
Establish appropriate documentation, procedures, and knowledge-sharing practices to reduce key-person dependency and ensure continuity of treasury operations.
Develop a scalable treasury operating model that can accommodate increased trading volumes, additional business lines, international expansion, and organizational growth.
Coordinate with Finance, Risk & Regulatory Affairs, external auditors, and other relevant stakeholders on treasury-related accounting, documentation, audit, and regulatory matters, as applicable.
Assess and implement treasury tools and reporting that improve visibility into cash balances, liquidity forecasts, financial exposures, hedge positions, and collateral requirements.

10+ years of progressive experience in corporate treasury, banking, capital markets, or financial risk management, including experience leading treasury or financial markets initiatives and advising senior decision-makers.
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. A CFA, CPA, CTP, or relevant graduate degree is an asset.
Experience building or improving treasury or financial risk management processes, including establishing controls, developing reporting, and training colleagues.
Experience implementing or improving treasury systems, banking platforms, cash forecasting tools, or financial risk reporting is an asset.
Experience in energy, power trading, commodities, or another business with significant exposure to financial markets is an asset.
Demonstrated expertise and deep understanding of foreign exchange markets, FX derivatives, and corporate FX risk management, as well as interest rate markets, interest rate derivatives, and balance sheet interest rate risk management.
Experience developing and implementing financial hedging strategies and risk management frameworks and advising treasury, finance, and C-suite-level decision-makers on the relevant use of these strategies.
Strong understanding of corporate liquidity management, cash flow forecasting, banking facilities, and balance sheet management.
Experience managing banking relationships with domestic and international financial institutions.
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with different business units, including Trading, Finance, Settlements, Risk & Regulatory Affairs and senior management.

As Practice Director, Shopify Commerce, you will own the technical vision, delivery excellence, and business development strategy for our enterprise Shopify Plus practice. You will lead a global team of architects, engineers, and solution consultants—shaping how we design, build, and scale mission-critical commerce platforms for our largest clients. Lead a practice at the forefront of enterprise Shopify Plus—working with some of the world’s most ambitious commerce brands.

Shape how our firm thinks about and delivers Shopify—building playbooks, growing a team, and influencing the direction of a high-growth practice.

Define and own the architectural patterns and best practices for enterprise Shopify Plus deployments, including headless/composable commerce, Shopify Functions, Markets Pro, and B2B capabilities.
Lead the design of end-to-end commerce ecosystems spanning Shopify Plus and adjacent enterprise systems—ERP (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia, Kenshoo), CDP/CRM (Salesforce, Segment, mParticle), PIM, OMS, and payment gateways.

Establish governance frameworks, risk mitigation strategies, and delivery KPIs tailored to the pace and complexity of commerce platform engagements. -
Act as a technical escalation point and actively unblock delivery teams, modeling the kind of senior leadership and decisiveness the practice requires.
Build, retain, and develop a high-performing team of Shopify architects, engineers, and solution leads—setting clear expectations, creating growth paths, and fostering a culture of technical excellence.

Own the technical narrative in the sales process: participate actively in discovery, solutioning, estimation, architecture design, and proposal development for Shopify Plus pursuits.
Partner closely with business development and account teams to identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities within existing Shopify Plus engagements.
Serve as a credible, senior technical voice in client-facing conversations—building trust, managing expectations, and positioning our practice as a strategic partner, not just a vendor.
Maintain and deepen relationships with Shopify’s partner and alliance teams, ensuring we are positioned for early access to new programs, beta capabilities, and co-sell opportunities.

Practice Development & Talent Growth

Mentor and coach Shopify architects, technical leads, and engineers across regions—actively investing in their growth and career trajectories.
Drive Shopify-specific certification and enablement programs (e.g., Shopify Partner certifications, Shopify Developer certifications) and build learning paths that keep the team at the forefront of platform innovation.
Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, solution playbooks, case studies, and reusable architecture assets that accelerate delivery and sales across the practice.

Utilization Optimization: Maintain or improve team utilization rates across all Shopify Plus engagements, targeting 70%+ blended team utilization.
Certification Growth: Drive 100% of the practice team to hold at least one Shopify Partner or Developer certification within 12 months.
Solution Quality: Ensure architectural integrity, scalability, and maintainability across all delivered Shopify Plus solutions—measured by client satisfaction scores and post-launch performance benchmarks.
Sales Pipeline Contribution: Actively participate in pursuits contributing to at least $8M in unweighted Shopify Commerce pipeline annually, with a target of closing $3M+ in new logos or significant expansions.
Individual Billability: Maintain a minimum of 50% individual billable utilization, balanced against the practice-building and sales activities inherent to this role.
Team Retention & Growth: Achieve 85%+ retention within the practice and maintain a pipeline of at least two internal candidates ready for promotion annually.

Must Have Qualifications

To be considered for this role, you must meet the following essential qualifications:

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology leadership within a consulting, systems integration, or agency environment—with at least 3–4 years specifically in Shopify Plus or a comparable enterprise commerce platform.
Deep, hands-on expertise in the Shopify Plus platform: Shopify Functions, Checkout Extensibility, Markets Pro, B2B, headless/composable commerce architectures, and the Shopify app ecosystem.
Strong command of the enterprise commerce technology stack surrounding Shopify Plus—including ERP integrations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia), CDPs (Segment, mParticle, Salesforce Data Cloud), PIM, OMS, and payment platforms.
Proven track record of participating in or leading sales pursuits, proposals, and client-facing solutioning conversations—comfortable owning a technical narrative in a competitive deal.
Experience building, leading, and growing distributed technical teams—hiring, mentoring, retaining senior talent, and creating cultures of technical excellence.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to operate fluently across executive, technical, and commercial audiences.

Shopify Partner Certification, Shopify Developer Certification, or Shopify Plus Certification (required or expected within 6 months of hire).
AWS/Azure/GCP Solutions Architect, TOGAF, SAFe, PMP, or equivalent—demonstrating both platform-level and enterprise architecture credentials.

CoCounsel Legal is Thomson Reuters' AI assistant for legal professionals. This role leads the part of it that makes it adaptable: the agent's ability to take on a customer's skills, connect to third-party systems, and remember what matters to each legal team.

As Director, you will lead multiple engineering teams building the core of the CoCounsel Legal product. Your teams will let law firms and corporate legal departments add their own skills, connect their own tools through MCP integrations, and make CoCounsel work the way they do.

You already build with coding agents and agent workflows, and you set the standard for how your teams do the same. You stay hands-on, make sound technical trade-offs, and plan strategically while the product and customer needs are still taking shape.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop multiple engineering teams, and build the leadership layer (managers and technical leads) as the scope grows. Own workforce planning, hiring, performance, calibration, and succession.
Own the engineering vision and delivery for how customers extend CoCounsel Legal. This includes custom skills and the tools to create, test, version, share, and retire them.
Lead the design and delivery of MCP and third-party integrations, so customers can connect their own systems and tools to the CoCounsel agent safely and at scale.

Partner with peers in Agent Core, Application Experience, Platform, and Corporate Integrations to keep CoCounsel coherent as a product.

AI-native ways of working: daily, proficient use of AI coding tools and agent setups to do engineering work, and experience setting team norms for verifying agent-generated work
Experience building integrations with third-party systems, and experience with MCP or comparable tool and plugin protocols
Experience building platforms that customers configure and extend, such as skills, plugins, extension frameworks, or workflow and automation features

Experience making sound technical trade-offs and resolving complex security issues, particularly where third-party access and customer data are involved
Experience evaluating agentic systems and building evaluation into the release process, working with science and subject-matter experts

Proven strategic planning: setting direction under ambiguity and re-planning based on evidence from working software and customers
Accountability for workforce planning, budget, and build-versus-buy decisions
Proficiency in Python and strong engineering fundamentals, including cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), CI/CD, and testing strategy
Understanding of the privacy, security, and compliance obligations of handling confidential and privileged customer data
Clear, persuasive communication with engineers, product partners, and senior business stakeholders

Experience building tools that let non-engineers create and improve agent behavior, such as skill or prompt authoring, test chats, and review workflows with versioning and rollback
Background in legal technology, or in enterprise software for legal, compliance, or risk functions, including customers who need confidentiality, ethical walls, and audit trails
Experience with enterprise administration and sharing models, such as groups, roles, org-level publishing, and usage reporting

This position is for an existing vacancy in a newly created role, as disclosed in accordance with the Ontario Employment Standards Act (ESA).

Company Overview:

Nexus Energy Inc. is a privately held energy company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, active in trading electricity across Eastern Canada, the Northeastern U.S., and Western markets, as well as providing power price risk management solutions to large commercial and industrial loads in Ontario. In addition, Nexus is actively working to develop a pipeline of renewable energy projects.

At Nexus, we foster a culture that values high performance, collaboration, and continuous development. You will join a passionate team that drives the business forward through innovation, accountability, and open communication.

Position Overview

Nexus Energy is seeking a Vice President, Treasury to build and lead its Treasury function. Reporting directly to the CEO, the VP will manage foreign exchange and interest rate exposures, execute hedging strategies, and oversee liquidity, banking relationships, and treasury operations.
The VP will partner with Trading, Finance, Settlements, and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to manage financial exposures and develop treasury processes and controls that support growth. Treasury will operate within the company’s Risk Policy and risk appetite, which are governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

We welcome senior corporate treasury professionals and senior banking or capital markets professionals with corporate advisory experience in hedging, funding, or liquidity. The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

What You Will Do

Foreign Exchange(FX) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring, and management of the company's foreign exchange exposures. Ensure FX exposures are managed appropriately in line with the company's Risk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate and execute appropriate FX hedging instruments and strategies, including forwards, swaps, options and structured hedging solutions, where appropriate to mitigate exposures arising from trading activities, operational cash flows, cross-border transactions and foreign currency-denominated assets and liabilities.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific FX risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor currency market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material FX risks, market conditions and potential hedging opportunities.

Interest Rate (IR) Risk Management
Lead the identification, measurement, monitoring and management of the company's interest rate exposures across its balance sheet and financing activities, in accordance with the company'sRisk Policy framework and in collaboration with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Evaluate the impact of changing interest rate environments on the company's financing costs, cash flows, liquidity and overall financial position.
Develop and maintain treasury-specific interest rate risk management processes and procedures, including exposure monitoring, hedge execution and operational controls, supporting the implementation of the company's Risk Policy framework and associated parameters as governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Monitor interest rate market developments and proactively advise senior leadership on material IR risks and provide strategic advice on interest rate positioning, hedging alternatives and financing considerations.

Balance Sheet Liquidity & Cash Management
Collaborate with Finance, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to monitor cash positions, funding requirements and liquidity buffers across the company's banking relationships and legal entities, ensuring sufficient liquidity to support ongoing trading activities, operational requirements and strategic initiatives.
Work closely with Finance, Trading, Settlements and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to anticipate material cash flow requirements, settlement obligations and potential liquidity pressures, developing and maintaining short-, medium- and long-term cash flow and liquidity forecasting frameworks.
Oversee liquidity requirements associated with trading activities, including collateral, margining, credit support arrangements and other working capital considerations.
Proactively identify opportunities to optimize cash utilization, funding efficiency, and returns on excess liquidity, as well as potential liquidity risks, and develop appropriate contingency funding and liquidity management plans.

Banking & Financial Institution Relationships
Own and manage the company's banking and financial institution relationships, acting as a primary point of contact for treasury-related matters. Develop strategic relationships with existing and potential banking partners, ensuring the company has access to appropriate banking products, credit facilities, and financial services.
Lead discussions and negotiations relating to banking arrangements, credit facilities, cash management solutions, trade finance, and other treasury-related services. Coordinate with senior leadership and the Finance team on financing requirements, facility renewals, credit negotiations, and broader funding initiatives.
Identify opportunities to diversify banking relationships, optimize banking costs, and improve access to financial products and services.
Advise the CEO and senior leadership on funding strategy and capital structure. Evaluate financing alternatives, including new or expanded credit facilities, to support trading activity, working capital, and business growth.
Partner with Finance and Legal to assess financing terms, collateral requirements, and covenant implications, and support the execution of approved financing initiatives.

Strategic Advisory & Risk Management Governance
Act as the company's senior treasury subject matter expert and provide strategic advice to the CEO and senior leadership on FX, interest rate, liquidity, and broader financial risk management matters, and recommend appropriate financial risk mitigation solutions that balance commercial objectives, risk tolerance, and market conditions within the company'sRisk Policy framework as defined and governed by Risk & Regulatory Affairs.
Work collaboratively with Risk &Regulatory Affairs, providing treasury and financial markets expertise to support the development, implementation, and ongoing maintenance of the company's Risk Policy, including financial risk exposures, hedging strategies, risk metrics, and practical risk management considerations. Overall Risk Policy ownership and governance will remain with Risk & Regulatory Affairs.

Cross-Functional Risk Identification & Management
Establish effective working relationships with Trading, Finance, Settlements, and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to ensure financial exposures arising from business activities are appropriately identified, communicated, monitored, and managed within the company's established Risk Policy framework.
Collaborate with Trading and Risk & Regulatory Affairs to understand current and anticipated trading positions, transaction structures, forecast cash flows, and associated FX and interest rate exposures, including financial risk and hedging considerations relating to customer transactions.
Work with Finance and Settlements to identify balance sheet exposures, financing requirements, foreign currency liabilities and other financial risks, ensuring timely identification of settlement-related exposures, currency requirements, cash movements and potential liquidity mismatches.
Partner with Risk &Regulatory Affairs to support the monitoring and management of financial risk exposures and associated hedging activities, providing treasury expertise and execution support as required.

Treasury Infrastructure, Process Development & Team Enablement
Establish and develop the company's treasury function, including the implementation of appropriate processes, systems, controls and reporting infrastructure. Assess existing treasury-related workflows and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, transparency, consistency and risk oversight.
Develop standardized processes for exposure identification, hedge execution, trade capture, confirmation, settlement, reconciliation and ongoing monitoring.
Work collaboratively with Finance and Settlements to strengthen internal treasury knowledge and capabilities. Cross-train and upskill existing Finance team members in treasury operations, FX and interest rate risk management, financial instruments and hedging methodologies.
Establish appropriate documentation, procedures, and knowledge-sharing practices to reduce key-person dependency and ensure continuity of treasury operations.
Develop a scalable treasury operating model that can accommodate increased trading volumes, additional business lines, international expansion, and organizational growth.
Coordinate with Finance, Risk & Regulatory Affairs, external auditors, and other relevant stakeholders on treasury-related accounting, documentation, audit, and regulatory matters, as applicable.
Assess and implement treasury tools and reporting that improve visibility into cash balances, liquidity forecasts, financial exposures, hedge positions, and collateral requirements.

What You Will Bring:

10+ years of progressive experience in corporate treasury, banking, capital markets, or financial risk management, including experience leading treasury or financial markets initiatives and advising senior decision-makers.
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. A CFA, CPA, CTP, or relevant graduate degree is an asset.
Experience building or improving treasury or financial risk management processes, including establishing controls, developing reporting, and training colleagues.
Experience implementing or improving treasury systems, banking platforms, cash forecasting tools, or financial risk reporting is an asset.
Experience in energy, power trading, commodities, or another business with significant exposure to financial markets is an asset.
Demonstrated expertise and deep understanding of foreign exchange markets, FX derivatives, and corporate FX risk management, as well as interest rate markets, interest rate derivatives, and balance sheet interest rate risk management.
Experience developing and implementing financial hedging strategies and risk management frameworks and advising treasury, finance, and C-suite-level decision-makers on the relevant use of these strategies.
Strong understanding of corporate liquidity management, cash flow forecasting, banking facilities, and balance sheet management.
Experience managing banking relationships with domestic and international financial institutions.
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with different business units, including Trading, Finance, Settlements, Risk & Regulatory Affairs and senior management.
Strong communicator with commercial acumen, negotiation skills and the ability to translate complex financial market risks into practical business recommendations. Possesses a keen ability to distil complex subject matter into digestible and actionable intelligence.
A strong team player who simultaneously demonstrates an ability to operate independently, exercise sound judgment, and influence decision-making at the senior leadership level. Experience developing talent, transferring technical knowledge, and fostering a collaborative, high-performance work

Define and own the architectural patterns and best practices for enterprise Shopify Plus deployments, including headless/composable commerce, Shopify Functions, Markets Pro, and B2B capabilities.
Lead the design of end-to-end commerce ecosystems spanning Shopify Plus and adjacent enterprise systems—ERP (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia, Kenshoo), CDP/CRM (Salesforce, Segment, mParticle), PIM, OMS, and payment gateways.
Evaluate and stay ahead of emerging Shopify platform capabilities (e.g., Shopify Audiences, Checkout Extensibility, Editions releases) and translate them into client-ready solutions and internal playbooks.
Serve as the practice’s ultimate authority on technical feasibility, scalability, and integration strategy for Shopify Plus engagements.

Delivery Leadership

Oversee technical delivery across global, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise Shopify Plus solutions, ensuring quality, performance, and client satisfaction at scale.
Establish governance frameworks, risk mitigation strategies, and delivery KPIs tailored to the pace and complexity of commerce platform engagements. -
Act as a technical escalation point and actively unblock delivery teams, modeling the kind of senior leadership and decisiveness the practice requires.
Build, retain, and develop a high-performing team of Shopify architects, engineers, and solution leads—setting clear expectations, creating growth paths, and fostering a culture of technical excellence.

Sales Engagement & Client Partnership

Own the technical narrative in the sales process: participate actively in discovery, solutioning, estimation, architecture design, and proposal development for Shopify Plus pursuits.
Partner closely with business development and account teams to identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities within existing Shopify Plus engagements.
Serve as a credible, senior technical voice in client-facing conversations—building trust, managing expectations, and positioning our practice as a strategic partner, not just a vendor.
Maintain and deepen relationships with Shopify’s partner and alliance teams, ensuring we are positioned for early access to new programs, beta capabilities, and co-sell opportunities.

Practice Development & Talent Growth

Mentor and coach Shopify architects, technical leads, and engineers across regions—actively investing in their growth and career trajectories.
Drive Shopify-specific certification and enablement programs (e.g., Shopify Partner certifications, Shopify Developer certifications) and build learning paths that keep the team at the forefront of platform innovation.
Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, solution playbooks, case studies, and reusable architecture assets that accelerate delivery and sales across the practice.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Utilization Optimization: Maintain or improve team utilization rates across all Shopify Plus engagements, targeting 70%+ blended team utilization.
Certification Growth: Drive 100% of the practice team to hold at least one Shopify Partner or Developer certification within 12 months.
Solution Quality: Ensure architectural integrity, scalability, and maintainability across all delivered Shopify Plus solutions—measured by client satisfaction scores and post-launch performance benchmarks.
Sales Pipeline Contribution: Actively participate in pursuits contributing to at least $8M in unweighted Shopify Commerce pipeline annually, with a target of closing $3M+ in new logos or significant expansions.
Individual Billability: Maintain a minimum of 50% individual billable utilization, balanced against the practice-building and sales activities inherent to this role.
Team Retention & Growth: Achieve 85%+ retention within the practice and maintain a pipeline of at least two internal candidates ready for promotion annually.

Must Have Qualifications

To be considered for this role, you must meet the following essential qualifications:

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology leadership within a consulting, systems integration, or agency environment—with at least 3–4 years specifically in Shopify Plus or a comparable enterprise commerce platform.
Deep, hands-on expertise in the Shopify Plus platform: Shopify Functions, Checkout Extensibility, Markets Pro, B2B, headless/composable commerce architectures, and the Shopify app ecosystem.
Strong command of the enterprise commerce technology stack surrounding Shopify Plus—including ERP integrations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia), CDPs (Segment, mParticle, Salesforce Data Cloud), PIM, OMS, and payment platforms.
Proven track record of participating in or leading sales pursuits, proposals, and client-facing solutioning conversations—comfortable owning a technical narrative in a competitive deal.
Experience building, leading, and growing distributed technical teams—hiring, mentoring, retaining senior talent, and creating cultures of technical excellence.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to operate fluently across executive, technical, and commercial audiences.

Preferred Certifications

Shopify Partner Certification, Shopify Developer Certification, or Shopify Plus Certification (required or expected within 6 months of hire).
AWS/Azure/GCP Solutions Architect, TOGAF, SAFe, PMP, or equivalent—demonstrating both platform-level and enterprise architecture credentials.

The team - Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst

Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst (Catalyst) empowers individuals and organizations to seize the opportunities and tackle the challenges of cybersecurity. Together with our partners and collaborators, we work to realize a vision of healthy democracies and thriving societies, powered by safe and secure digital technologies.
Through our groundbreaking training and certification programs; unique commercial acceleration programs for cybersecurity start-ups and scale-ups; first-of-its-kind cyber range; wide-ranging public education programs; and influential policy interventions, the Catalyst helps drive Canada’s global competitiveness in cybersecurity.
The Catalyst is a not-for-profit corporation owned and operated by Toronto Metropolitan University and based in Brampton, ON. Hybrid work schedule with expectations of 2 days in the Brampton offices.

The opportunity

Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst at Toronto Metropolitan University is looking for a strategic, operational, and relationship-driven leader to lead its Defence Sector Growth portfolio, focused on the rapid acceleration and integration of small and medium-sized businesses into defence supply chains.

As the Director, you will play a key role on the senior leadership team, leading the strategy, development, delivery, and long-term sustainability of the portfolio.
You'll have the opportunity to:

Drive economic development outcomes for Canadian businesses:
Identify emerging opportunities within Canadian and allied defence supply chains, drive cyber compliance readiness and other supplier requirements, and shape market access programming to drive economic outcomes benefitting Canadian companies.
Build strategic partnerships:
Build meaningful relationships with key government procurement and industry support departments and agencies, including the Defence Investment Agency, BDC and PSPC, the Canadian Armed Forces, and the defence industrial base, including leading defence businesses and industry partners.
Lead impactful programs:
Design and deliver initiatives that guide Canadian small and medium-sized businesses through complex defence procurement processes, achieve required cyber certifications, and increase access to Canadian and allied defence supply chains..
Grow and sustain the portfolio:
Identify new business opportunities, develop partnerships and funding proposals, and secure investments to support long-term program sustainability.
Lead people and performance:
Oversee portfolio operations, budgets, strategic outcomes, and team development.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced leader to bring together government, industry, and Canadian businesses to strengthen Canada's defence ecosystem, help shape the future of the national security supply chain, and drive generational economic growth for Canadian businesses.

Completion of a post-secondary degree in business, public administration, supply chain management, operations, or a related field.
A minimum of 7 years of progressively senior experience planning and implementing organization-wide strategies, including stakeholder management, business development, and financial management, with proven leadership experience in organizational strategy, change management, program management and organizational growth.
Experience in a leadership role, managing staff and external resources and planning and managing budgets.
Experience in defence supply chains, government procurement, defence industry engagement, national security or related fields, including leading complex programs, initiatives or partnerships, and working within or closely with the Canadian defence and national security ecosystem (e.g., government departments and agencies, the Canadian Armed Forces, the Department of National Defence, or defence industry organizations).
Extensive knowledge of defence procurement policies and practices and established professional relationships within this ecosystem.
Experience developing and managing large government-funded programs, and building and implementing fee-for-service programs, including developing services and products for small and medium-sized businesses.
Knowledge of financial and project methodologies, principles and practices; excellent analytical and program evaluation skills; and excellent networking and relationship-building skills, including the ability to work with stakeholders from different areas and with different agendas.
